subject: Mega 5-Bullet Friday — Some Favorite Life Advice for 2025

bullets.title: A message for the New Year
bullets.note:
from [Brandon Stanton](https://tim.blog/2018/06/18/brandon-stanton-humans-of-new-york/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit), creator of [Humans of New York](https://www.humansofnewyork.com/). This relates to something he and I have texted about often: attention. How should you think about protecting your own attention in 2025? If you don’t have attention, the time and money you have matter little. Attention is the mother resource. Brandon’s post was first written earlier this year, but it’s more relevant every day.

​[**Coach Christopher Sommer’s email to me**](https://x.com/tferriss/status/1826691823789641750)**.** [Coach Sommer](https://www.instagram.com/christophersommer1/?hl=en) is a former US National Team gymnastics coach and the creator of [GymnasticBodies](https://www.gymnasticbodies.com/).

**“**[**Why You Should Seek More Awe in the New Year**](https://tim.blog/2024/01/24/awe/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit#content)**”** by [Ashley Stimpson](https://www.ashleystimpson.com/). Every time I’ve done a [past-year review (PYR)](https://tim.blog/2021/12/27/past-year-review/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit#content), a pattern emerges: peak positive emotional experiences are correlated to awe at least 70% of the time. For at least the past 3–5 years, this has been so consistent that I often determine what big blocks to schedule in the new year based on potential for awe. The payoffs include [time dilation](https://www.instagram.com/reel/C2cdhDQO7_S/?igsh=MTk4M3lhc2diZjVjNA%3D%3D) and, more broadly, traversing the miraculous canvas of full human experience. Friends have asked me why I do silent retreats in nature, why I love ski touring, why I hunt once in a blue moon, or why I am deeply interested in psychedelic science and [psychedelic-assisted therapies](https://saiseifoundation.org/). If I had to sum it all up in one word, it would be: Awe. But what exactly is “awe,” and how can we embrace more of it? I haven’t found a better article exploring these topics than Ashley Stimpson’s “[Awestruck](https://hub.jhu.edu/magazine/2023/winter/science-of-awe-psychedelics/),” featured in [_Johns Hopkins Magazine_](https://hub.jhu.edu/magazine/2023/winter/science-of-awe-psychedelics/), so I asked for permission to publish on my blog, which was graciously granted. I hope you find it as thought-provoking as I did.

**“**[**Masters of Love**](https://www.theatlantic.com/health/archive/2014/06/happily-ever-after/372573/)**.”** (_The Atlantic_). [Alternate link](https://archive.is/2024.03.12-072741/https://www.theatlantic.com/health/archive/2014/06/happily-ever-after/372573/). This is the best article on courtship, love, and dating that I’ve read in years. It’s not only well-researched and full of memorable insights, it’s very actionable and gives labels to concepts you can use. Don’t let the subheadline throw you; it’s terrible. “Science says lasting relationships come down to—you guessed it—kindness and generosity” would make me think, “Yeah, duh. I’ll skip this one.” But the article is much more interesting and helpful than the subheadline implies.

**“**[**The Most Important Question of Your Life**](https://markmanson.net/question)**”** by [Mark Manson](https://tim.blog/2022/12/30/mark-manson/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit#content). I could see reading this once a week. Excellent reminders all around.

**“**[**So you wanna de-bog yourself**](https://www.experimental-history.com/p/so-you-wanna-de-bog-yourself)**”** by [Adam Mastroianni](https://substack.com/@experimentalhistory). I only just found Adam, but his writing is some of the most hilarious—and helpful—I’ve seen in a long time. Really worth the read. Big thanks to Crazy B for sending this to me.

**“**[**63 principles**](https://nabeelqu.co/principles)**”** by [Nabeel S. Qureshi](https://x.com/nabeelqu). Nabeel is currently a stealth startup founder but was previously at Palantir. He has been a visiting scholar in AI at the Mercatus Center as well as an Emergent Ventures awardee.

**“**[**101 Additional Advices**](https://kk.org/thetechnium/101-additional-advices/)**”** by [Kevin Kelly](https://kk.org/). Regular readers know that I consider Kevin one candidate for [the real-world most interesting man in the world](https://tim.blog/2023/04/26/kevin-kelly-excellent-advice-for-living/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit#content).

**“**[**You can’t hoard life**](https://ckarchive.com/b/68ueh8hkxrx6lukq88gqmtz7vxkkk)**”** by [Oliver Burkeman](https://www.oliverburkeman.com/), author of [_Four Thousand Weeks: Time Management for Mortals_](https://www.amazon.com/Four-Thousand-Weeks-Management-Mortals/dp/B08XZY5ZF7/). Hat tip to [Chris Williamson](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9G5dXlMGMf8) for sending this to me.

bullets.title: “When life gets tough, some of us feel that we’ve lost the game and life has won. But life isn’t trying to defeat you. Life isn’t even a participant—the game is yours.” — Mo Gawdat in Solve for Happy _
